steps.content: Your body has been transformed into something unknown and is trapped in an otherworld device. Sending you to the murder scene of "the gods" would be no easy task.
But this technical expert clearly managed to do it.
With just a few simple commands, you feel a strange fluctuation, and your body becomes lighter.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: You are now successfully digitalized. I can transfer you to the last place she lingered. There happens to be a suitable device there.
While you were still brainstorming what you need her to do, Moore already realized them.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Be careful at the scene. We don't even know what "the gods" are, let alone what that Sinner means by "killing them."
[Arrival]
The speed of traveling through the data channel is as fast as Moore fulfilling the request, but when you reach the terminal, you realize that perhaps your sense of time is distorted.
"You" have been casually placed in a dim room. It's already night outside, and directly in front of you is a huge whiteboard covered in otherworldly language.
Before you can make out the text, your vision gets blocked by something. You instinctively reach out, but quickly realize it's no use.
Drip-drip...
They're blood drops. The killing has already happened.
You hear Rise gasp.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: The scene must be terrifying. How awful.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Rise, connect with the sheriff for investigation.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...I'll be right back.
The intern's footsteps fade away.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Did you deliberately send her away? How kind of you, Chief.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all, she's just a young intern. No matter how reliable she is, a murder scene is too much for her to stomach.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Huh? Should I be feeling something?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hehe, it's fine, I'm still half asleep. Don't worry. Investigate to your heart's content, Chief. I'll decode and analyze the data from the scene.
A halo appears before your eyes. It appears to be some kind of decoding process. Following Moore's instructions, you try to touch it with your hand.
Investigation 1
Moore sends back the images with translations added and bloodstains removed. Now you can see more clearly.
Investigation 2
The content on the left looks like some regular art design workflows, though some parts are hard to translate.
It seems to include some self-encouraging phrases.
Investigation 3
The content on the right is meant to categorize music tracks, which is easier to understand. There seems to be a rough hand-drawn doodle in the lower right corner.
Investigation 4
Curious, you zoom in. The content on the screen is somewhat puzzling. It seems to be the death scene of some kind of bird, which stands out from the rest of the content.
It just looks like the work of ordinary people.
Nothing indicative of the powerful world-commanding gods that 000 had mentioned.
[Investigation Ends]
A buzzing sound suddenly rings out. You see a message transmitted to this device.
"What time will you be back? Should I leave the door open for you?"
You feel a sense of suffocation.
This place is rather ordinary, much like a meeting room in a small company in Eastside.
So much so that it feels like the one who died here was not a "god" but merely a common person that you would encounter in the streets.
She doesn't appear but lets you hear her voice.
Hehe, I was wondering when you'd notice me.
Why do you look so unhappy? Angry that I peeked at your investigation?
Or mad that I committed a crime here?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I make it a habit to stay alert around dangerous people, especially someone as ruthless as you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You killed a person here, didn't you?
Not a "person," Chief. They're not from your world, not your kind, and they have no feelings for you.
They never care about what you care about, so why should you worry about their lives? Do you cry for the Corruptors you kill?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Do you think I would still believe anything you say?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After kidnapping, deceiving, and using me?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Confining me here won't stop me from finding out the truth. I'm not alone.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: No problem. I've hacked into the surveillance cameras at the scene. The data is connected, Chief. The surveillance footage is now streaming to you in real-time.
[Switch to static]
Wait!
The surveillance camera doesn't follow 000's command but instead points to the ground on the other side.
[Duck death scene]
Sigh... At least let me clean up the scene first. The blood and gore will make you hate me even more.
A god. To be precise, it's the corpse of a god I killed. Sorry, I'm a bad, ruthless woman.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Isn't this just a duck? And a goofy-looking one at that.
Are you questioning my intelligence? How dare you. Don't use your low-dimensional mind to imagine the true form of a god.
What's wrong with looking like this? It's cute. Don't judge a god by its appearance.
What a fuss! This is the god who created your game. Don't believe me? Look!
Hehe.
You're stunned and completely at a loss on how to take in the situation before you.
Is she telling the truth? Setting aside the whole "god" thing, do the creatures of this world really look like this?
You sigh. This farce is so absurd that you want to pinch your face to see if you can wake up from it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So it's just killing ducks. Do whatever makes you happy.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I don't have time to spare. Send me back.
No, no... they just look cute, but they're not actually goofy. Don't think any less of them.
No, you can't fall for her trick. You immediately steady your mind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This bit of footage proves nothing. It could also be faked. You have no credibility with me anymore.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is a completely staged murder scene. You're wasting my time.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Tell me the truth. What did you do to our world?
Ah, what a stubborn log you are. You used to be more fun and relaxed. Why are you so...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I don't believe a word you say.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Moore, what do you make of this?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Chief, I've thoroughly searched all the data available at the scene. The surveillance footage and recordings have not been tampered with. But there is indeed the possibility of other alterations, perhaps done hastily, leaving some traces of anomalies.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I suspect there are deeper secrets at this murder scene that have been altered, but I've yet to confirm the specifics.
You see 000 raise an eyebrow with interest.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: So it's a trick after all.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Additionally, I've retrieved and decoded a large amount of audio-visual data from the deceased's phone currently accessed by you. Some data is locked and inaccessible, but the available content indeed matches the situation in DisCity.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It is worth noting that some of the content has been abnormally modified recently. These modifications perfectly correspond to the recent apparitions in DisCity.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: In other words, whether it's ducks or gods, there is indeed a certain kind of being at this scene with the power to alter our world, whose might is beyond our imagination.
...No wonder you were snatched away from me. Turns out it's an expert who can grasp the key points right away.
Moore, right?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Thanks for the compliment. Helping Chief is my job.
Is that so... Then please help him. Our Chief still seems confused.
steps.female_content: Is that so... Then please help her. Our Chief still seems confused.

steps.content: She turns back to you.
It doesn't matter what the gods look like. I turned them into these funny creatures for your sake.
If you saw the real death scene, you'd flare up immediately.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: ...What does the real scene look like?

steps.content: Disturbing images flash through your mind. What's really behind those two toys...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who really got killed here? What are these ducks really...
Who do you think they are? Gods? Ducks? Or <color=#fb9259>people</color> like you?
Hehe, doesn't matter anymore. No matter what they once were, this is what they are now. Their existence has changed.
Since I killed two gods and took the power to control their form and voice, I've already replaced them.
And these are just the first two. Once I get them all...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I won't let you do that.

steps.content: Then come over to my side? Be my companion, and we can usurp the gods together. The power will be yours by then.
If you don't trust me to play with the world, then you do it. You have my earnest invitation.
Why? I know you're a flexible person who's ready to try new things. Why not give me a chance?
Think of it like this: this is a one-stop solution to resolve all problems and realize all wishes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm no stranger to this kind of bait and I won't fall for it.
Are you really going to refuse? Aren't you tempted, even a little? You've never been curious about my proposal? Don't you want to try the second option?
...You won't stand with me no matter what?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Say no more. I will do everything I can to stop you.
Hahaha, of course, I know. I was just teasing you!
You would never choose or be tempted by me. You are the unwavering Chief who would never betray your true self.
But is this really your true self? Or is it designed by someone else for you?
A smile shows on her face.
I won't make it hard for you. I know you are not in a position to make any choice right now. You can only go down the path dictated for you. That's fine.
Just think of it as a game. The ones who died are just toy ducks. You came here for a silly adventure. Your only enemy is a shallow, daydreaming oddball of a Sinner.
If I can't be your teammate, being your opponent would be fun too. It's a game, after all, which is meant to be enjoyed.
Once everything settles, you will be liberated too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I am already free and under no one's control. I don't need your liberation.
Alright, alright, time's almost up. I'm off.
As much as I want to stay with you, the next god is already waiting for me to deliver the killing blow. I can't delay any longer.
Game on! Whether you join me, try to stop me, or just travel around for fun in this otherworld, it's up to you.
Since you believe so much in your own free will.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Chief, should we go after her?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: ...Do you believe the absurd things she said?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hmm... I don't see anything wrong with them?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: "The world is a huge game, and the gods set all the rules." Haha, this concept has also been brought up in old movies. As a programmer, I quite like this way of understanding the world.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Except for the gods' appearance... They're really too cute, completely different from what I imagined.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: So, Chief, do you believe what she said?
No matter how ridiculous her words are, it's very likely that there is some strong link between the two worlds.
You slowly understand the things written on that whiteboard, which bear uncanny resemblance to your world. If she can really seize all the gods' authority...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We must stop her, but...
With your paper-thin body trapped in the device... what can you do... the next target...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Don't worry, I've already pinpointed the most likely target she's after next.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: According to her game world theory, the world where DisCity is located is numbered as 5732. This is the developer's world.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: On the computers of the two murdered ducks, I found an online space which serves as a kind of group chat for developers. Many IDs are having real-time discussions, and indeed, they are all related to our world.
As she speaks, she shows you some group chat texts.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Interesting. Just as that Sinner was about to leave, a new discussion started in the developers' group:

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Is the next target this "Code Duck"?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Very likely. If I were her, I would also target this duck first.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: After all, "programming" authority is very important.
You break into a sweat.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Are we able to catch up to her?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: At the very least, we can't let her gain more power.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Rise has already pinpointed her destination. I'll find a transferable target device for you.
Everyone is doing their best to assist you, you must find 000 and stop her plan.
At least, find her before she succeeds again.
